key_insight: PureVision adds geometry-aware supervision to medical vision-language models so they better preserve lesion anatomy and phenotype relationships in visual representations.
clinical_relevance: This could improve how AI systems localize lesions and characterize complex multi-phenotype findings in radiology tasks like VQA and report generation.
method: PureEyes learns latent visual spaces with ideal spatial distributions that encode anatomical hierarchies and phenotype subclass relations.
PureNeurons uses those latent positions to selectively aggregate lesion-specific anatomical and phenotypic evidence.
The framework is designed to address sparse lesion cues that standard semantic-only alignment may miss.
evidence_signal: The paper reports improvements on LIDC-IDRI, CBIS-DDSM, and 3DReasonKnee, with better lesion grounding and phenotype characterization in visual question answering and radiology report generation.
watch_item: Results are reported on specific benchmark datasets, so broader clinical reliability and performance across scanners, populations, and workflows still need external validation.
paper_title: Geometry-Supervised Visual Representation Learning for Multi-Phenotype Lesion Interpretation in Medical VLMs
